effect: Signs the law, then publishes a note explaining which parts of it the signature did not mean.
available_to: A president, a bill he cannot afford to veto, and a legal office with a printer.
counter: Read the statement into the record, fund only what the statute says, and let a court decide what the signature bought.

confused_with.tell: The pocketveto kills the bill; the signaway keeps the bill and kills the part of it he dislikes.

senses: The signing statement: a message issued alongside a signature, claiming a constitutional objection to part of the law just signed - a veto that arrives after the bill is already law.

It works because a signature is the only thing the Constitution actually requires. The statement carries no vote and binds no court, but it is a public instruction to the agencies that have to enforce the statute, and instructions are followed more often than they are litigated.
example: *"He signed the oversight bill with a **signaway** attached, and the agency read the note instead of the statute."*
